## Test report: 202605 branch (cisco-8000, amd64)

I tested this PR on **202605**. I built **cisco-8000** in a Microsoft internal sonic-buildimage 202605 tree. Its sonic-linux-kernel submodule is the public `202605` branch (`288cc3645d5d`). All three images come from the same sonic-buildimage commit:

| Build | Change | Image version |
|---|---|---|
| Baseline | none | `internal-202605.186089081-1d8266d407` |
| A | sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel#641 + the `rules/linux-kernel.mk` change from #30172 | `kernel-dbg-pr641.186113249-19b9381ce1` |
| B | A + this PR (same diff, applied to 202605 lines 151-152) | `kernel-dbg-pr641-fix.186113257-b54257957a` |

### Test steps
1. Apply sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel#641 on sonic-linux-kernel 202605. Declare `LINUX_KERNEL_DBG` as a derived package of `LINUX_HEADERS_COMMON` in `rules/linux-kernel.mk`, as #30172 does.
2. B only: apply this PR.
3. Build `target/sonic-cisco-8000.bin` and compare `target/` with the baseline file by file.
4. Check the `apt -y install` line in the rootfs build log (`sonic-cisco-8000.bin__cisco-8000__rfs.squashfs.log`), run `unsquashfs -lls fs.squashfs usr/lib/debug` on the image, and compare the image and rootfs sizes.
5. Check that the published `-dbg` package still matches the kernel in the image: the GNU build-id of `vmlinux` against `/boot/vmlinuz-*` in the image, and of every module debug file against the shipped modules.

### Results
| | Baseline | A (without this PR) | B (with this PR) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `-dbg` package in `target/debs/trixie/` | no | yes, 817 MB | yes, 817 MB |
| Kernel packages installed by `apt -y install` | `-unsigned` | `-dbg` and `-unsigned` | `-unsigned` |
| `sonic-cisco-8000.bin` (bytes) | 2,440,071,151 | 3,748,845,551 | 2,439,835,631 |
| rootfs (mksquashfs filesystem size) | 758 MB | 2,501 MB | 758 MB |
| `/usr/lib/debug` in the image | none | 3,848 files, 5,038 MiB | none |
| `vmlinux` build-id matches the image kernel | n/a | yes | yes |
| Module build-ids matching | n/a | 3,840 of 3,840 | 3,840 of 3,840 |

No other package in `target/` changed. The rootfs build log of B:
```
+ sudo LANG=C DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive chroot ./fsroot-cisco-8000 apt -y install ./initramfs-tools-core_0.142_all.deb ./initramfs-tools_0.142_all.deb ./linux-image-6.12.41+deb13-sonic-amd64-unsigned_6.12.41-1_amd64.deb
```
The rootfs build log of A:
```
+ sudo LANG=C DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive chroot ./fsroot-cisco-8000 apt -y install ./initramfs-tools-core_0.142_all.deb ./initramfs-tools_0.142_all.deb ./linux-image-6.12.41+deb13-sonic-amd64-dbg_6.12.41-1_amd64.deb ./linux-image-6.12.41+deb13-sonic-amd64-unsigned_6.12.41-1_amd64.deb
```
master shows the same problem: build [1248403](https://dev.azure.com/mssonic/build/_build/results?buildId=1248403) (#30172, broadcom) installs the `-dbg` package, and its rootfs grows from 616 MB to 2,359 MB compared with build 1248688.

I also checked the new package selection in a shell with dummy files. Without a `-dbg` package it selects the same packages as before. With one, it drops only the `-dbg` package. Without any kernel image package, the `set -e` script still stops at this step.

### Conclusion
With this PR, the image is the same as without sonic-net/sonic-linux-kernel#641, and the `-dbg` package is still published for crash debugging. Without it, every image grows by about 1.3 GB. This PR must be merged before the sonic-linux-kernel submodule update that brings in #641.

Rebased onto current master, preserving the existing F070 patch and valid-XML behavior (head `f2ffd7b5c`).

Two distinct CI failures were identified:
* `check-file` rejects the intentional edit to protected `src/sonic-config-engine/minigraph.py`. This requires the repository-maintainer approval/exception; rebasing or rerunning cannot resolve that policy gate, and no workflow protection has been weakened.
* Azure build 1249560, Elastictest plan `6ad27c4f7fd582d5dacc9d4b`, failed `pc/test_lag_member.py::test_lag_member_traffic` with "Arp info for portchannel is not correct" on VPP `vlab-vpp-02`. This is a separate integration failure; no baseline equivalence has been established, so it is not being labeled unrelated or fixed.

Local execution of the full XML regression module is unavailable on this Windows host because the Linux SONiC `swsscommon` dependency is missing. Fresh PR-context CI should provide platform validation after this push.

For F063, we can keep the original structure and existing uses of `args.P` / `args.N`. No helper functions or password-flow changes needed.

Replace the credential defaults:

```python
parser.add_argument('-P', default=os.environ.get("SONIC_PASSWORD"),
                    help='login password')
parser.add_argument('-N', help='new password')
```

`-N` has no default and no environment variable; a new password is used only when it is passed explicitly. Then fail immediately after parsing if the login password is missing, before any telnet connection:

```python
args = parser.parse_args()

if not args.P:
    parser.error("login password required: use -P or SONIC_PASSWORD")
```

In the forced-password-change branch (reached only when the `Current password:` prompt appears, e.g. with `CHANGE_DEFAULT_PASSWORD=y`), fail if `-N` was not provided:

```python
if not args.N:
    parser.error("new password required: use -N")
```

This removes the hardcoded fallbacks, keeps CLI precedence over the environment for `-P`, and rejects missing passwords. No `NEW_PASSWORD` / `SONIC_NEW_PASSWORD` build-system plumbing is needed; random generation is optional hardening rather than necessary for this narrowly scoped fix.

### Review update (commit dd6027c9)

**Fix verification.** A real malicious pickle (gzip and raw, with an `exec` reducer that writes a probe file) was run against Scapy `8e08cbf7` with the patch series applied.

| Path | Baseline (0001+0004) | This PR (0001+0004+0005+0006) |
|---|---|---|
| `python -m scapy -s evil.session` | payload executes | `option -s not recognized`, exit status 1, no execution |
| `interact(argv=["scapy","-s",path])` | payload executes | exit status 1, no execution |
| `load_session()` / `update_session()` | payload executes | `AttributeError` (removed) |
| `init_session(path)` (old positional signature) | payload executes | rejected, no file read |
| installed wheel (`scapy.main:interact` entry point) | n/a | `-s` rejected, no execution; normal start works |

**Test fix.** The original `-s` regression test passed for the wrong reason: `interact()` parses `argv[1:]`. It now passes a program name in `argv[0]` and asserts exit code 1 and the getopt error. A mutation check shows it fails against vulnerable code and passes with the fix. The upstream `interact_emulator()` argv placeholder is restored, so the `-d` case is exercised again. UTscapy `regression.uts` reports the same 26 environment-only failures on the baseline and on this PR; there are no new failures.

**Cache-key gate.** `SONIC_CACHE_RECIPE_VER_BASELINE` is updated to the new `slave.mk` hash, without a `SONIC_CACHE_RECIPE_VER` bump, as the gate advises for non-recipe changes. The other P0 items the gate reports (`BMC_NOS_ACCOUNT_USERNAME`, `BMC_ROOT_ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`, `CHANGE_DEFAULT_PASSWORD`, `DBGOPT`, `IMAGE_TYPE`, `MASTER_CRI_DOCKERD`, `MASTER_KUBERNETES_VERSION`, `USERNAME`) are existing RFS cache-key gaps on master. This PR doesn't introduce them; they are escalated only because it touches one line of `build_debian.sh` (removing `apt-get install python3-scapy`). Adding password values to cache keys or waivers is outside the scope of this security fix. Maintainer guidance on how to handle them for this gate would be appreciated.

**Still pending before ready-for-review:** Linux image build check (Debian `python3-scapy` absent from the host, patched wheel provides `/usr/local/bin/scapy`), the docker-orchagent build, and warm-reboot validation.

Agreed on settling the extensible wire format upstream. [FRR PR 21863](https://github.com/FRRouting/frr/pull/21863) is the right place to finalize that design. @tahmed-dev @pbrisset, could you help take this forward and decide on the upstream fix?

Removed the commented-out LOCAL route-selection block in [`fdd5f35ee`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/fdd5f35eeec19acc288e2da3837b284c87060184). Moving the filtering policy into `dplane_fpm_sonic.c` is a good direction, but it changes where the behavior is enforced and requires focused route/FPM validation. I will handle this in a follow-up PR.

> **3. FPM build switch**

Agreed that a configure option could improve standalone build and test coverage. This spans configure logic, Debian packaging, and test enablement, so I am deferring it from the current PR.

> **4. suppress-FIB delay**

I authored the original patch. The startup template and dynamic bgpcfgd path currently issue bare `bgp suppress-fib-pending`. Dropping patch `0065` requires moving the `50 ms` value into both paths and updating the generated-configuration coverage. I plan to handle this change and its verification in a separate PR.

> **5. Series header**

Addressed in [`fdd5f35ee`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/fdd5f35eeec19acc288e2da3837b284c87060184). The header now records the pristine FRR 10.7.1 SHA.

`safe_strerror()` is included in [`fdd5f35ee`](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/commit/fdd5f35eeec19acc288e2da3837b284c87060184). I kept the operation switch exhaustive because the compiler warning provides useful detection when a later FRR release adds an operation.

> **7. Private FPM numbers**

I compared the values with latest public sonic-swss master. The 140-based EVPN-MH range, 1000-3001, encap type 101, and most SRv6 attributes are mirrored. Message types 4000/4001 and SID-list attributes 5-7 have no public `fpmsyncd` mirror. A complete registry therefore needs a cross-repository ownership and consumer review, so I am deferring it from the current PR.

Findings
[P1] Make can skip Bazel after source edits
The new archive rules depend only on .platform and _BAZEL_BASE archives. After the first build, editing a source used by the Bazel container leaves those prerequisites unchanged. Make considers the existing .gz current and skips bazel run, potentially carrying stale container contents into the final image. This affects release and debug builds. [Bazel archive rules](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1507-L1517)
The outer Make’s -B does not solve this: it is not forwarded through Docker or supplied to the inner Make command. Make should invoke Bazel whenever the archive is requested, allowing Bazel to check its own inputs. [Worker invocation](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L682-L781)

[P1] Sharing output_user_root can fail or abort builds
Both the system Bazel configuration and P4RT point to one output root under the default host-shared cache. This applies to P4RT even when the new container option is disabled. [System configuration](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/tools/bazel/slave.bazelrc#L12), [P4RT override](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/src/sonic-p4rt/Makefile#L30-L31)
Two failure cases follow from the pinned Bazel implementation:
- Different host users: the first user creates the output root; the second user’s Bazel process exits because its UID does not own that directory. Making the parent world-writable does not satisfy Bazel’s ownership check. [Bazel ownership check](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/cpp/blaze_util_posix.cc#L490-L521)
- Concurrent slaves using the same UID: default slaves mount each checkout at /sonic, so Bazel selects the same output base. Source tracing shows that separate PID namespaces can cause another server to start there; replacing the shared PID file can terminate the active server and abort its build. [Workspace mount](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L367-L372), [Bazel output-base selection](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/cpp/blaze.cc#L1334-L1340), [PID-file watcher](https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/blob/6.4.0/src/main/java/com/google/devtools/build/lib/server/PidFileWatcher.java#L39-L107)
Give users and concurrent slaves isolated output roots. Both configuration paths need the change.

[P2] Bazel images lose the load targets required by Make consumers
Filtering Bazel images out of DOCKER_IMAGES also removes them from DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS. The loader rule creates targets only for that explicit list. [Filtering](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1375-L1376), [Loader construction](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1591-L1608)
Once a release image uses Bazel, building its ordinary Make debug image—or another Make container that lists it in _LOAD_DOCKERS—requests target/<image>.gz-load and fails because no loader exists. Include the Bazel image lists when creating load targets. [Consumer prerequisites](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/slave.mk#L1523-L1528)

[P2] Existing cache directories are changed to mode 0777
The new shell expression evaluates as (test directory || create directory) && chmod. Consequently, chmod also runs when the directory already exists.
A user who points SONIC_BAZEL_CACHE_SOURCE at an existing mode-0700 directory has it changed to 0777 during Makefile parsing, even with the Bazel container option disabled. Preserve existing permissions and apply creation permissions only to newly created directories. [Cache setup](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L248-L249)

[P2] The Trixie guard misses configuration-file values
The guard is in the root Makefile, which does not read rules/config.user or rules/config.organization. The worker loads those files later and passes the resulting flag to the slave. Thus, setting the flag to y through configuration bypasses a restriction that the same CLI value triggers; direct worker invocations also bypass it. [Root guard](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile#L42-L49), [Configuration loading](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/3518d5fc7aff2b04cb1a4490c266168adddbfe1d/Makefile.work#L167-L169)
Validate the effective configuration in the worker or slave. This is a confirmed enforcement gap; it does not mean every Bookworm phase necessarily runs a Bazel target.

I suggest four focused changes in this PR. The key design is: Make hands each requested container to Bazel, while Bazel owns dependency checking and caching.

1. Always let Bazel check the container

Add a normal phony prerequisite to both Bazel archive rules. Keep the .gz targets as real file targets. Current rules

.PHONY: FORCE_BAZEL
FORCE_BAZEL:

$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/,$(SONIC_BAZEL_DOCKER_IMAGES)): $(TARGET_PATH)/%.gz: .platform FORCE_BAZEL \
	$$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/,$$($$*.gz_BAZEL_BASE))
	$(HEADER)
	bazel run //dockers/$*:write_$*.gz $(LOG)
	$(FOOTER)

Apply the same prerequisite to the debug rule.

The writer must also:

  • Produce deterministic archive bytes, including compression metadata.
  • Leave the existing archive and its timestamp untouched when the bytes are identical.
  • Atomically replace the archive when its contents change.

This gives the intended behavior:

Situation | Result -- | -- No source changes | Bazel checks its graph; archive timestamp stays unchanged Source changes, same resulting contents | Bazel rebuilds affected actions; archive stays unchanged Container contents change | Archive is replaced; downstream image can rebuild

For developers, default the host cache to a user-owned location such as $HOME/.cache/sonic/bazel. For CI, configure a persistent directory dedicated to each runner UID.

Keep only these settings in slave.bazelrc:

common --repository_cache=/bazel_cache/repository_cache
common --disk_cache=/bazel_cache/disk_cache

Remove the shared output_user_root setting. I would also drop this PR’s P4RT Makefile hunk, preserving its existing manual /bazel override for users who explicitly configure it. Normal P4RT builds would inherit the persistent disk/repository caches and use slave-local output state. P4RT change

For directory preparation:

  • Move it from Make parsing into slave setup.
  • Create a missing user directory with mode 0700.
  • Preserve existing ownership and permissions.
  • If the configured directory is unusable, report that and run with local caches.

This retains cached action outputs across runs. A new slave still reconstructs its analysis and extracted workspace; that is the tradeoff for isolating server state. Bazel supports disk-cache reuse across checkouts. Bazel cache documentation

A persistent output root can be considered later, with an exclusive lock held for the entire slave lifetime.

3. Restore the existing Docker loaders

Add the Bazel groups to DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS before its static pattern rule. Current loader list

DOCKER_LOAD_TARGETS += $(addsuffix -load,$(addprefix $(TARGET_PATH)/, \
	$(SONIC_BAZEL_DOCKER_IMAGES) \
	$(SONIC_BAZEL_DBG_DOCKER_IMAGES)))

The existing loader can then serve Make-built debug images and containers that depend on a Bazel-built base. Validate that the Bazel writer produces the archive format and image tags expected by docker-image-load.

4. Enforce the Trixie restriction inside the slave

Keep the root check for early CLI feedback, and add the authoritative check in slave.mk after configuration files are loaded:

ifeq ($(BUILD_WITH_BAZEL_WHEN_AVAILABLE),y)
ifneq ($(BLDENV),trixie)
$(error BUILD_WITH_BAZEL_WHEN_AVAILABLE=y requires a trixie slave)
endif
endif

That covers configuration-file values and direct worker invocations while preserving this PR’s current Trixie-only policy. Current root guard

For a future mixed-distro build, I would select Bazel only inside the Trixie slave and let other slaves continue using Make. That is a broader behavior change than closing this guard gap.

Thank you for your comments @lguohan !

As for your concerns:
> [P1] Make can skip Bazel after source edits

I'm happy to apply your comments, but also please note that in the common case (`BAZEL_MIN_READINESS=true BLDENV=trixie make target/docker-sysmgr.gz`), the Make build will still overcache. Note that this also happens in the current Make-based targets.

The only way to make this not happen is to make the catch-all rule a `.PHONY`, and I think that is too big a change for this PR.

> [P1] Sharing output_user_root can fail or abort builds
> [P2] Existing cache directories are changed to mode 0777

Yep, you're absolutely right. I've just removed the shared output base, and replaced it with a per-user cache directory (with mode 0700).

> [P2] Bazel images lose the load targets required by Make consumers
> [P2] The Trixie guard misses configuration-file values

Great points, implemented both!


Also, please note that I've replaced the binary "is Bazel enabled" flag with the more nuanced "BAZEL_MIN_READINESS" toggle, so that users can decide whether they want to consume all available Bazel builds, or just the stable ones.
